episode_title: 198: UX resume myths about the ATS, with Workday UX director and hiring manager Patrick Neeman
question: Why should UX professionals avoid using two-column layouts on resumes for applicant tracking systems?
transcript_excerpt: Two-column layouts break in applicant tracking systems because most ATS use OCR (optical character recognition) technology to convert PDFs or Word documents into text the system can understand. The OCR reads column one, then sees column two as a continuation of the same line, converting all carefully formatted information into one big line of text. This technology has largely remained unchanged since 1992, so the two-column layout does not work for ATS parsing, though a single-column format allows the resume to be properly read by both the ATS and human recruiters.

question: What is the six-second eye tracking study about recruiter resume review time?
transcript_excerpt: The Ladders conducted an eye tracking study approximately fifteen years ago that found recruiters spend an average of six seconds looking at a resume. This study is often cited as evidence of how quickly recruiters make initial judgments. However, Patrick Neeman notes that in practice, he takes about a twenty-second glance to assess whether it looks like a resume or case study, and judges based on design quality before making reject or interview decisions.

episode_title: 198: UX resume myths about the ATS, with Workday UX director and hiring manager Patrick Neeman
question: What are the key misconceptions candidates have about applicant tracking systems and hiring?
transcript_excerpt: Patrick Neeman identifies three major ATS misconceptions: First, that companies are really good at hiring when they often lack clear hiring criteria and pull generic job descriptions from the internet without editing them. Second, that all applicant tracking systems have advanced AI, when in fact many are not technologically advanced and lack dedicated teams. Third, that recruiters are highly organized when in reality they get buried under large volumes of resumes and make quick rejections based on initial design impressions rather than thorough review.

episode_title: 198: UX resume myths about the ATS, with Workday UX director and hiring manager Patrick Neeman
question: How can generative AI help UX designers optimize their resumes for applicant tracking systems?
transcript_excerpt: Generative AI is particularly effective at rewording resume and case study content to match the specific keywords that applicant tracking systems are configured to filter on. Rather than manually rewriting content, candidates can use AI tools to improve their resumes and PDFs to help get ahead of other applicants by fitting the keyword requirements that ATS systems look for.

question: What resume design elements pass the initial recruiter screening at Workday?
transcript_excerpt: For enterprise hiring, resumes that stand out in the first six seconds use clean layouts, good typography, strong line spacing, and clear hierarchy of information. Patrick Neeman emphasizes that he does not want resumes to be too creative for enterprise roles, focusing instead on strong information architecture and readability rather than artistic design choices that might work for consumer-facing positions.
